text:
Alicia M: I'm about to sign off for the night but leaving an incident on /v1/generate that still has elevated 5xxs. handing off to @Miguel R as primary. quick summary below.

Miguel R: on it, grabbing context. can you drop the runbook links and any temporary mitigations you applied?

Alicia M: yes — tl;dr: upstream cache evictions caused backend noise; we've throttled burst traffic and enabled a short-lived suppression for noisy downstream retries. customer impact: increased latencies for a minority of requests and ~2.5% 5xx rate over 10m. not widespread but noisy for a few customers.

Alicia M: mitigations applied: 
- prefix cache warming triggered for high-traffic prefixes
- rate-limit on internal retry worker (temp)
- alerts escalated to P1 where 5xx > 1% over 5m, but we might need to bump for noise

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-12T22:12:34Z — Alert: high_5xx_rate_v1 triggered (channel: eng-oncall).

Sam (SRE): noted. if it's downstream-induced spikes, we should avoid paging everyone for transient noise. propose raising the alert firing threshold from 1% -> 3% for the duration of the mitigation window, and open a suppression ticket.

Priya (infra): agree. We should also adjust the alert to require sustained window 10m instead of 5m while we triage, so we don't page on short flares.

Miguel R: I'm taking primary. thanks Alicia. I'll own updating alert config and the suppression ticket. leaving a quick checklist in the thread.

Miguel R: checklist: 
1) Update alert config in Prometheus manager
2) Create incident suppression with expiry (2h)
3) Notify support + CS for impacted customers
4) Runbook pointer: https://internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/5xx_incident (see section: downstream-noise)

Nora (Support): copying CS here — I've prepared a brief customer message for the 3 affected accounts, ping me if you want it sent.

Miguel R: making the config change now. command I ran:```sh
# update alerting rule temporarily
kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap alert-rules --patch '\n{"data":{"high_5xx_rate_v1.yaml":"threshold: 0.03\nwindow: 10m\n"}}'\n```

Sam (SRE): can you paste the diff? want to ensure we didn't accidentally change routing.

Miguel R: pasted the rule snippet below:```yaml
- alert: high_5xx_rate_v1
  expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{route=~"/v1/generate.*",code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route=~"/v1/generate.*"}[5m]))) > 0.03
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "High 5xx rate on /v1/generate"
```

Alicia M: adding an explicit note — this is TEMPORARY. we'll revert to 1% and 5m after mitigations and postmortem. create a follow-up task to revert.

Miguel R: created suppression: SUP-1769994321 in incident tracker, expires in 2h. linked to incident. also updated the on-call rotation to notify both primary and secondary on pages > critical.

Priya (infra): routing policy change noted. Are you leaving the fallback model variant in place?

Miguel R: yes, fallback to quantized-v1 is enabled for low-priority tiers. no customer-facing model changes.

Nora (Support): sending customer note now to the three accounts. cc: @Alicia M for review.

Alicia M: one more: if the 5xx crosses 7% or we see error patterns tied to auth failures, escalate to ENG-PI and page the full escalation bridge.

incident-bot: Alert update — high_5xx_rate_v1 resolved for now (last firing 1769994540).

Miguel R: monitoring  — 5xx currently at 1.8% and trending down after throttles. leaving a watch on it for 90m.

Sam (SRE): nice work. please drop a short post-incident note in #postmortems with root cause and the decision to temporarily relax thresholds. include the revert task ID.

Miguel R: will do. creating postmortem stub and assigning to the infra-oncall triage. PM: revert task RT-1769994333 created.

Alicia M: thanks team — I'm off, Miguel is primary and Sam is secondary for escalation. Miguel, please call if you need anything. :thumbsup:

Miguel R: thanks, good handoff. I'll update the shift board and close the thread after monitoring window. :eyes:
